function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to help you find a place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a national chain that delivers.

---

## 1️⃣ Start With Your Location  
If you’re comfortable sharing your city or ZIP code, I can give you more tailored suggestions. If not, use these general methods:

| Method | How it Works | Pros | Cons |
|--------|--------------|------|------|
| **Google Maps / Apple Maps** | Search “cake delivery near me” or “bakeries” | Shows nearby options, ratings, hours | Might miss smaller, independent shops |
| **Yelp / TripAdvisor** | Look for “cakes” or “bakeries” | Reviews & photos | Some listings may be outdated |
| **Local Facebook Groups / Nextdoor** | Post a request or browse posts | Community recommendations | Requires a Facebook account |

---

## 2️⃣ Major Online Delivery Platforms  
These apps deliver from many local bakeries and grocery stores. Just enter your address and filter by “cakes” or “desserts.”

| Platform | What It Offers | Tips |
|----------|----------------|------|
| **DoorDash** | Local bakeries, grocery stores, specialty shops | Use “Specialty Food” filter; check delivery fees |
| **Uber Eats** | Same as DoorDash | Look for “Dessert” category |
| **Postmates** | Often includes niche bakeries | Check “Custom Orders” option |
| **Instacart** | Grocery delivery (often has cake options) | Great for last‑minute orders |
| **Amazon Fresh** | Fresh groceries + some cake options | Good for bulk orders or pre‑packaged cakes |

---

## 3️⃣ Specialty Cake Shops & National Chains  

| Shop | Where to Order | Highlights |
|------|----------------|------------|
| **Goldbelly** | Website | Curated selection from famous bakeries across the U.S. (great for special occasions) |
| **Bakeology** | Website | Custom cakes, vegan & gluten‑free options |
| **Magnolia Bakery** | Website & app | Classic American pastries & cakes |
| **Baked by Melissa** | Website | Bite‑size cupcakes (great for parties) |
| **The Cake Shop** | Website | Custom designs, seasonal flavors |
| **Cakes.com** | Website | Custom orders, design templates |

> **Tip:** For custom designs, most sites let you upload a photo or choose from templates. Be sure to check the turnaround time—some take 48–72 hrs.

---

## 4️⃣ Local Independent Bakeries  
Often the best quality and freshest ingredients. Find them via:

- **Google Maps** – look for “best rated” or “handmade”
- **Instagram** – search hashtags like #YourCityBakery or #YourCityCakes
- **Local Food Blogs** – they usually list top picks

When you find a bakery, call or visit their website to confirm:
- **Delivery area** (some only serve within a certain radius)
- **Minimum order** (many require a minimum spend)
- **Payment options** (cash, card, or online)

---

## 5️⃣ Ordering Tips for a Smooth Experience  

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Order Early** | Cakes often need 24–48 hrs prep time |
| **Specify Allergies** | Let the baker know about nut, dairy, or gluten allergies |
| **Ask About Packaging** | Ensure the cake arrives intact (especially if it’s a custom design) |
| **Check Reviews** | Look for recent photos and comments about delivery |
| **Confirm Delivery Time** | Some services allow you to schedule a specific slot |

---

## 6️⃣ Quick Starter List (U.S. Only)  

| City | Recommended Bakery / Service |
|------|-----------------------------|
| New York | **Magnolia Bakery** (online), **Goldbelly** |
| Los Angeles | **Baked by Melissa**, **Postmates** |
| Chicago | **The Cake Shop**, **DoorDash** |
| Houston | **Bakeology**, **Instacart** |
| Miami | **Goldbelly**, **Uber Eats** |

*(If you’re outside the U.S., just replace the city with your own and use the same platforms—they’re available in many countries.)*

---

### Bottom Line  
- **Use a delivery platform** for convenience and variety.  
- **Call local bakeries** for custom orders and to confirm details.  
- **Plan ahead**—especially for custom cakes or special dietary needs.

Happy cake hunting! 🎂
